# LLMS.txt — f1rc Architecture Map (starter)

Purpose: hardware/firmware facts an AI assistant can't safely infer from source
alone. Read this before generating driver, ISR, or memory-handling code
(see CLAUDE.md section 3). Extend this file whenever a new peripheral, board,
or target is added — do not let it go stale.

Status: STARTER DOC, drafted 2026-07-27 from apps/car/car-bsp source
(no CubeMX .ioc is checked into the repo — it was removed; this file is now
the source of truth for pin/clock/DMA facts until/unless one is reintroduced).
Currently only covers the `car` app / STM32F411 target.

## Target: `car` app

- MCU: STM32F411CEU6 (LQFP48), Arm Cortex-M4F
- Flash: 512 KB @ 0x08000000
- SRAM: 128 KB @ 0x20000000
- HAL package: STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver, vendored under bsp/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver
  (confirmed present: HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA / HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback,
  i.e. this HAL version supports IDLE-line DMA reception — no need to hand-roll it)

### Clock configuration (apps/car/car-bsp/car_bsp.c: car_bsp_system_clock_config)

- Source: HSI (internal 16 MHz RC), PLL bypassed (RCC_PLL_NONE)
- SYSCLK = HCLK = PCLK1 = PCLK2 = 16 MHz (all dividers = DIV1)
- FLASH_LATENCY_0
- NOTE: this is a conservative/development clock config, not the part's rated
  max (100 MHz via PLL). Any timing-sensitive calculation (baud rate, DMA
  throughput, systick) must assume 16 MHz unless this config changes.

### RTOS

- FreeRTOS via CMSIS-OS2 API (osKernelInitialize/osKernelStart in car_bsp.c)
- PendSV priority is fixed at 15 (lowest) — required by FreeRTOS, do not change
  (apps/car/car-bsp/stm32f4xx_hal_msp.c: HAL_MspInit)
- apps/car/car-bsp/inc/FreeRTOSConfig.h:
  - configPRIO_BITS = 4 (16 priority levels, 0=highest .. 15=lowest)
  - configLIBRARY_MAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY = 5
  - **ISR-safety rule**: any interrupt handler that calls a FreeRTOS
    `...FromISR` API (queues, semaphores, task notifications) MUST be
    configured at NVIC preemption priority >= 5 (i.e. numerically 5-15).
    Priorities 0-4 are "above the kernel" and must never call FreeRTOS APIs.
  - Existing precedent: DMA2_Stream2_IRQn is set to priority 5 in
    uart_interface_init() — treat 5 as the standard priority for any new
    UART/DMA IRQ that needs to touch FreeRTOS primitives from ISR context.

### Peripheral / pin map

| Peripheral | Pins | AF | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| USART1 | PA9 = TX, PA10 = RX | AF7 | apps/car/car-bsp/stm32f4xx_hal_msp.c: HAL_UART_MspInit |

USART1 config (apps/car/car-bsp/car_bsp.c: car_bsp_init):
- Baud 115200, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity, no HW flow control,
  16x oversampling, mode TX+RX
- Wired up as `context->cmd_uart` via `uart_interface_init(...)` — this is the
  "command" UART, used for host/PC <-> car communication (see comms/hldc,
  comms/simpliciti for the protocol layers running over it)

### DMA stream/channel assignments (STM32F411 DMA request mapping)

| Request | Controller | Stream | Channel | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| USART1_RX | DMA2 | Stream2 | 4 | **in use** (apps/car/car-bsp/car_bsp.c) |
| USART1_RX (alt) | DMA2 | Stream5 | 4 | available if Stream2 is needed elsewhere |
| USART1_TX | DMA2 | Stream7 | 4 | not currently used — TX is blocking/polling (HAL_UART_Transmit) |

USART1 is on APB2 → its DMA requests only route through **DMA2** (DMA1 serves
APB1 peripherals: USART2/3, UART4/5, SPI2/3, I2C1/2/3, TIM2-7). Don't assign a
DMA1 stream to a USART1 request — it doesn't exist in the request mapping.

### Repo driver convention

- Peripherals are wrapped in a `xxx_interface_t` struct bundling the raw HAL
  handle(s) + a function-pointer callback, e.g.
  `comms/interfaces/uart_interface/{inc/uart_interface.h,uart_interface.c}`:
  `uart_interface_t { UART_HandleTypeDef huart; DMA_HandleTypeDef hdma_rx;
  on_uart_if_recv_t on_recv; }`
- `xxx_interface_init()` takes raw HAL config enums as parameters rather than
  hiding them behind another abstraction — callers pass HAL constants directly
  (e.g. `UART_WORDLENGTH_8B`).
- No malloc/free anywhere near ISR-adjacent code (CLAUDE.md hard rule) —
  buffers used by DMA/ISR must be static, either file-scope `static` or fields
  on the `xxx_interface_t` struct itself.

### Known gaps / TODO for this file

- No CubeMX .ioc in-repo; if one is reintroduced, prefer it as source of truth
  and reduce this section to a diff/summary.
- Only the `car` app / STM32F411 target is documented. `comms/simpliciti` and
  other apps/targets are not yet covered here.
- Error handling for HAL_UART_Init/HAL_DMA_Init failures is currently a bare
  `while(1) {}` spin (uart_interface.c) — not a fault registers/CFSR mechanism,
  just noted here so it isn't mistaken for intentional recovery logic.
